name: Bangkok
summary: Gilded temples on the river, street food on every corner, rooftop bars and the giant Chatuchak market, with Ayutthaya and the floating markets a day trip away.

months.note: Peak cool, dry season and lowest humidity, so hotels cost more. Chinese New Year can fall late Jan or Feb and fills Yaowarat.
Still dry high season, warming up. Chinese New Year often lands this month.
Hot season starts and crowds thin, but heat and humidity build.
Hottest month. Songkran water festival (13-15 April) packs Silom and Khao San Road, and prices spike.
Rainy season begins with afternoon storms; low-season hotel deals start.
Green season: short daily downpours, fewer tourists, discounted rooms.
Rainy, but European summer holidays bring a bump in visitors.
Wet and humid, with steady summer-holiday traffic.
Wettest month; streets can flood. Hotel prices are at their lowest.
Rain tapers off late in the month and high-season prices return. Chinatown's Vegetarian Festival is usually late Sep or Oct.
Dry season and high season begin. Loy Krathong fills the riverbanks with floating krathongs.
Driest, most pleasant month and peak season. Book ahead for Christmas and New Year.

tips.title: Visa-free stay is now 30 days
tips.body: From 15 September 2026, visa-exempt tourists from about 60 countries (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the EU) get 30 days, down from 60. One extension can be requested from Thai immigration.

tips.title: Fill in the TDAC before you fly
tips.body: Every foreign visitor must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival. It's free on the official site, tdac.immigration.go.th; skip look-alike sites that charge a fee.

tips.title: Passport validity and proof of funds
tips.body: Your passport needs 6 months left and a blank page. Immigration may ask for an onward ticket and 10,000 baht per person (20,000 per family).

tips.title: No tourist entry fee yet
tips.body: The planned 300-baht tourism fee had no start date as of mid-2026. If it starts, it's expected to be added to air fares or the TDAC, not paid at immigration.

tips.title: ATMs charge foreign cards 220 baht
tips.body: Most Thai ATMs charge a flat 220 baht per withdrawal (AEON about 150). Take out larger amounts less often and always choose to be charged in baht.

tips.title: Tipping is optional
tips.body: Not expected at street stalls or where a 10% service charge is on the bill. Otherwise 5-10% at sit-down restaurants, round up taxis, and 50-100 baht after a massage.

tips.title: Plugs and voltage
tips.body: 220V, 50Hz. Most sockets take Type A, B and C plugs. Check your chargers say 100-240V.

tips.title: Temple and Grand Palace dress code
tips.body: Cover shoulders and knees at temples. At the Grand Palace no shorts or sleeveless tops. Take your shoes off before entering temple halls.

tips.title: Respect the monarchy
tips.body: Criticising the royal family, even in a shared post, can bring a long prison sentence. Never deface royal images, including on banknotes.

tips.title: Vapes are illegal
tips.body: Owning or using any vape or e-cigarette is illegal, with fines of 5,000-30,000 baht and possible detention. There's no tourist exemption.

tips.title: Cannabis now needs a prescription
tips.body: Since 23 June 2025, buying or using cannabis flower needs a Thai medical prescription. Recreational use is illegal again.

tips.title: "Grand Palace is closed today"
tips.body: Friendly strangers near the palace may say it's closed and wave you into a cheap tuk-tuk tour that ends at gem or tailor shops. Ignore unsolicited help and check opening hours yourself.

tips.title: Taxis, Grab and the metro
tips.body: Insist on the meter in taxis; walk away from flat-fare quotes. Grab and Bolt show the price upfront. The MRT takes contactless Visa and Mastercard; the BTS Skytrain still needs a Rabbit card or a single ticket.

tips.title: Dengue and mosquitoes
tips.body: Dengue is around all year and peaks in the rainy season (about June to October). Use repellent, especially in the daytime. Ambulance: dial 1669.

tips.title: Street food and water
tips.body: Pick busy stalls that cook to order and serve it hot. Drink bottled or filtered water: the tap water is treated, but old building pipes can contaminate it.

tips.title: Beat the heat
tips.body: Highs are 32-36°C all year. Sightsee in the mornings, drink lots of water, and check the AQI in the dry season if you have asthma.

places.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
places.blurb: Home of the Chakri kings since 1782. The compound holds Wat Phra Kaew and the Emerald Buddha, Thailand's most sacred image.
places.tip: Ignore anyone outside saying it's closed today: it's a scam.

places.name: Wat Pho
places.blurb: Home of the 46 m gold-leaf Reclining Buddha and the traditional centre of Thai massage teaching.

places.name: Wat Arun
places.blurb: The Temple of Dawn on the Thonburi bank, its central prang covered in porcelain mosaic. Best at sunset from across the river.

places.name: Tha Tien to Wat Arun ferry
places.blurb: A short shuttle boat across the Chao Phraya from Tha Tien pier, by Wat Pho, to Wat Arun.

places.name: Wat Benchamabophit (Marble Temple)
places.blurb: King Rama V's temple built of Italian Carrara marble, pictured on the back of the 5-baht coin.

places.name: Jim Thompson House
places.blurb: Teak houses and Asian art collection of the American silk trader who vanished in Malaysia in 1967.

places.name: Golden Mount (Wat Saket)
places.blurb: A man-made hill topped by a golden chedi, about 300 steps up, with 360-degree views over old Bangkok. Great at sunset.

places.name: Khao San Road
places.blurb: Bangkok's famous backpacker street of guesthouses, bars, street food and stalls. Liveliest at night.

places.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
places.blurb: One of the world's biggest weekend markets: thousands of stalls of clothes, crafts, plants, antiques and food.
places.tip: Weekends only. Go early before the heat, and haggle.

places.name: Bike and canal tour
places.blurb: Guided bike rides through Chinatown alleys and Thonburi's canal-side villages, finishing with a longtail boat ride. Co van Kessel is the long-running operator.

places.name: Sompong Thai Cooking School
places.blurb: Cooking school on Silom Soi 13 near BTS Chong Nonsi. Classes start with a market visit.

places.name: Rajadamnern Stadium
places.blurb: Bangkok's oldest purpose-built Muay Thai stadium, opened in 1945.

places.name: Lub d Bangkok Siam
places.blurb: Hostel opposite MBK at BTS National Stadium, with dorms and private rooms.

places.name: Bangkok National Museum
places.blurb: Thailand's largest museum, partly in the old Front Palace, covering Thai art and history from prehistory on.

places.name: Karim Roti Mataba
places.blurb: Long-running Thai-Muslim shop on Phra Athit Road, known for roti, mataba and curry.

places.name: The Deck
places.blurb: Riverside restaurant at Arun Residence looking straight across to Wat Arun. Popular at sunset.

places.name: Yaowarat (Chinatown) street food
places.blurb: After dark Yaowarat Road turns into one of Bangkok's busiest street-food strips: seafood, noodles, dim sum and desserts.

places.name: Siam Paragon
places.blurb: Big luxury mall at BTS Siam with an aquarium, cinema and a huge food hall.

places.name: Wat Ratchabophit
places.blurb: Rama V-era temple known for its Benjarong-tiled cloister and Gothic-style chapel interior.

places.name: Loha Prasat
places.blurb: The Metal Castle at Wat Ratchanatdaram: a tiered building with 37 metal spires, the only one of its kind left.

places.name: Red Sky
places.blurb: Rooftop bar on the 55th floor of Centara Grand at CentralWorld, under a red-lit arch.

places.name: Ayutthaya
places.blurb: The old Siamese capital (1351-1767), 80 km north of Bangkok. Its temple ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Damnoen Saduak & Maeklong Railway Market
places.blurb: A half-day trip pairing the busy Damnoen Saduak floating market with the Maeklong market, where stalls fold back as the train passes.

places.name: Siri Heritage Bangkok Hotel
places.blurb: Three-star old-city hotel with Siamese touches and a small pool, near the Grand Palace and Khao San.

places.name: Longtail boat canal tour
places.blurb: Longtail boats leave from piers like Tha Chang and run through Thonburi's canals past stilt houses and temples.

places.name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
places.blurb: Contemporary art centre opposite MBK with galleries on a spiral ramp. Free; closed Mondays.

places.name: MBK Center
places.blurb: Eight-storey budget mall with more than 2,000 shops: phones, clothes and souvenirs.

places.name: Erawan Shrine
places.blurb: Hindu shrine to Brahma at the Ratchaprasong junction, where worshippers pay classical dancers to perform.

places.name: Jodd Fairs Ratchada
places.blurb: Night market behind Central Rama 9 near MRT Phra Ram 9, with food stalls and shops. It took over from the old Talad Neon market.
places.tip: Moved from Rama 9 to Ratchada, next to Thailand Cultural Centre MRT, in 2025.

places.name: Sukhumvit Soi 11 bars
places.blurb: Nightlife lane with the Above Eleven rooftop and Havana Social, a Cuban speakeasy you enter through a phone booth.

places.name: Sampeng Lane
places.blurb: Narrow wholesale lane through Chinatown packed with stalls of accessories, toys, fabrics and trinkets.

places.name: Wat Traimit (Golden Buddha)
places.blurb: Home of a 5.5-tonne solid-gold Buddha found under a plaster shell in 1955, plus a Chinatown heritage museum.

places.name: Lumphini Park
places.blurb: Central Bangkok's big green space, with a lake, jogging paths and wild monitor lizards.

places.name: Silom Thai Cooking School
places.blurb: Popular budget cooking school off Silom Road; half-day classes start with a market visit.

places.name: Sky Bar at Lebua
places.blurb: Open-air bar on the 63rd floor of lebua at State Tower, made famous by The Hangover Part II.

places.name: Amphawa Floating Market
places.blurb: Weekend canal-side market popular with Thai visitors, known for grilled seafood sold from boats and evening firefly boat trips.

places.name: Riva Surya Bangkok
places.blurb: Four-star boutique hotel on the river with a riverside pool, near Khao San and the Grand Palace.

places.name: Ruam Tai
places.blurb: Southern Thai restaurant near Wang Lang Market serving fiery curries from 6 am.

places.name: Som Tam Jay So
places.blurb: Famously fiery Isan som tam spot on Soi Phiphat 2, packed with office workers at lunch.

places.name: Or Tor Kor Market
places.blurb: Upscale fresh market next to Chatuchak, known for top-quality fruit, curries and northern Thai food stalls.

places.name: Tom Yum Goong Banglamphu
places.blurb: Street-side shop on Kraisi Road near Khao San famous for creamy tom yum with big river prawns.

places.name: Airport to the city
places.blurb: From Suvarnabhumi: the S1 bus to Khao San, the Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai, or a metered taxi from the official queue.

itineraries.title: 3 days in Bangkok on a budget
itineraries.summary: Temples and the Grand Palace by the river, the Marble Temple, Jim Thompson House and Khao San Road, then a bike and canal tour, a cooking class and Muay Thai.
itineraries.creator: thebrokebackpacker

items.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
items.note: BTS to Mo Chit. Don't be afraid to haggle; try coconut ice cream.

items.name: Wat Pho
items.note: 5-10 min walk from MRT Sanam Chai. Wear shoes you can slip off.

items.name: Grand Palace
items.note: 5-10 min walk from Wat Pho.

items.name: Marble Temple
items.note: BTS Phaya Thai, then walk or tuk-tuk. Creator: go at dawn if you're a morning person.

items.name: Jim Thompson House
items.note: 20 min walk from BTS Siam. No photos inside.

items.name: Golden Mount
items.note: Bus 8 from Victory Monument.

items.name: Khao San Road
items.note: Pad Thai and a beer on a plastic stool.

items.name: Bike and canal tour
items.note: MRT to Itsaraphap. Lunch included; ends with a longtail boat ride.

items.name: Sompong Thai Cooking School
items.note: BTS to Sukhumvit.

items.name: Muay Thai at Rajadamnern
items.note: 7 min walk from Khao San Road.
items.priceNote: third class 1,000 THB; ringside 2,500 THB (creator: $65 VIP)

items.name: Lub d Bangkok Siam
items.note: Creator's best hostel pick. Or Thanabhumi (budget) or the Marriott Surawongse (luxury).
items.priceNote: per night, private double; dorms cheaper (date-dependent)

itineraries.title: 3 days in Bangkok, local-approved
itineraries.summary: Old-town temples and the National Museum, sunset at Wat Arun and Chinatown street food, then Chatuchak, the Golden Mount and a rooftop bar, with an optional day trip.
itineraries.creator: bucketlistly

items.name: Bus S1 from the airport
items.note: Straight to Khao San Road. Taxi is about 300 THB plus a 50 THB airport fee.

items.name: Grand Palace
items.note: Ignore tuk-tuk drivers who say it's closed. Elephant pants to cover up cost about 150 THB.

items.name: Karim Roti Mataba
items.note: Lunch on Phra Athit: beef panaeng with yellow rice, and the mataba they're known for.

items.name: Wat Arun at sunset
items.note: Then a drink at The Deck across the river.

items.name: Khao San Road
items.note: Check it out, but don't stay too long.

items.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
items.note: MRT to Chatuchak Park or Kamphaeng Phet.

items.name: Golden Mount at sunset
items.note: 318 steps up.

items.name: Loha Prasat
items.note: Best after dark when it's lit up.

items.name: Red Sky rooftop bar
items.note: Dress code: no flip-flops. Or Nest in Sukhumvit, or Wanderlust in Thonglor.

items.name: Ayutthaya day trip
items.note: Wat Chai Watthanaram, Wat Maha That, Wat Phra Si Sanphet.

items.name: Damnoen Saduak & Maeklong tour
items.note: Creator: Damnoen Saduak is more or less a tourist trap; the train market is the fun part.

items.name: Siri Heritage Bangkok Hotel
items.note: Creator's top pick. Or Niras Bankoc hostel (budget), Sala Rattanakosin (high-end).

itineraries.title: The perfect 3 days in Bangkok, plus a day trip
itineraries.summary: Grand Palace, Wat Pho and a private longtail through the canals, then malls, shrines and Sukhumvit bars, Chinatown and the Golden Buddha, a cooking class and Sky Bar.
itineraries.creator: theplanetd

items.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
items.note: Open 8:30 am to 3:30 pm.

items.name: Wat Pho
items.priceNote: 300 THB per adult (creator: 100 THB with free water)

items.name: The Deck
items.note: Lunch with great drinks and a view of Wat Arun.

items.name: Private longtail through the canals
items.note: Stops at a small floating market.
items.priceNote: creator: 1,000 THB for the whole boat

items.name: Khao San Road
items.note: One of the cheaper places to drink and shop. Sunset at the Golden Mount, a 20 min walk.

items.name: Riva Surya Bangkok
items.note: Creator's Banglamphu pick. Or Okura Prestige (Sukhumvit), Royal Orchid Sheraton (riverside, where they stayed).

items.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
items.note: Sat-Sun 9 am to 6 pm. Everything is super cheap.

items.name: Jim Thompson House
items.note: BTS National Stadium.

items.name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
items.note: Closed Mondays.

items.name: Erawan Shrine
items.note: BTS Chit Lom.

items.name: Night market
items.note: Creator's pick was Talad Neon, which has closed. Jodd Fairs in Rama 9 is the nearest equivalent.

items.name: Sukhumvit Soi 11 bars
items.note: Above Eleven rooftop, then Havana Social: get the phone-booth code from the Cubano sandwich seller.

items.name: Sampeng Lane
items.note: Never accept the first price.

items.name: Wat Traimit (Golden Buddha)
items.note: MRT Hua Lamphong. Creator recommends adding the museum.
items.priceNote: 100 THB Buddha only; 200 THB with museum (creator: 40/140 THB)

items.name: Lumphini Park
items.note: Paddle boats; 20 THB more for bread to feed the fish.

items.name: Silom Thai Cooking School
items.note: Morning class includes a market tour; night class 900 THB.

items.name: Sky Bar at Lebua
items.note: Or Moon Bar at Banyan Tree.

items.name: Amphawa Floating Market
items.note: Creator's favourite floating market. Van from the Southern Bus Terminal. Weekends.

itineraries.title: One-day Thai food tour of Bangkok
itineraries.summary: Eat your way through four regions of Thai food in one day: southern curries for breakfast, Isaan som tam for lunch, northern dishes at Or Tor Kor and tom yum goong for dinner.
itineraries.creator: markwiens

items.name: Ruam Tai
items.note: Southern Thai breakfast near Wang Lang Market: sour curry with taro stems, dry beef curry, salted fried fish. Open 6 am-8 pm.
items.priceNote: creator: dishes 40-50 THB; meal about 300 THB

items.name: Som Tam Jay So
items.note: Isaan lunch: som tam, minced catfish laab, grilled pork neck, sticky rice. Gets packed at lunch; 8:30 am-4:30 pm.

items.name: Or Tor Kor Market
items.note: Northern Thai at the Pen Jan stall: gaeng hanglay, sai oua sausage. Great place to try durian too.

items.name: Tom Yum Goong Banglamphu
items.note: Central Thai dinner: tom yum goong, shrimp omelet, morning glory with crispy pork. 9 am-6:30 pm.
